examples.en: The more strongly the teacher speaks, the more I feel like pushing back.

examples.ko: 부모님이 공부하라고 하면 오히려 반발심만 커져요.
examples.en: When my parents tell me to study, it only makes me want to resist more.

examples.ko: 규칙이 너무 많으면 직원들의 반발심을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If there are too many rules, you can provoke resistance from the employees.
Out of defiance, I deliberately did the opposite.

examples.ko: 반발심으로 시작한 일이 의외로 잘 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Something I started out of defiance unexpectedly worked out well.

examples.ko: 반발심에 나도 모르게 큰 소리로 대꾸했어요.
examples.en: Out of defiance, I talked back loudly without thinking.

explain: '반감'과 비슷하지만 반발심은 시키는 대로 하기 싫고 맞서고 싶은 마음에 가까워요. '반발심이 들다/생기다/커지다', '반발심을 사다'처럼 자주 써요. 강요나 억압을 느낄 때 자연스럽게 나오는 마음이에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '반감' (antipathy), but 반발심 is closer to the urge to push back and refuse to do as told. It is often used as '반발심이 들다/생기다/커지다' and '반발심을 사다'. It comes up naturally when you feel forced or pressured.

examples.en: In winter, temperature and heating costs are almost inversely related.
Exercise and body weight are not always inversely proportional.

examples.ko: 속도와 걸리는 시간은 서로 반비례하는 관계예요.
examples.en: Speed and travel time are inversely proportional to each other.

examples.ko: 케이크 크기가 같으면 사람 수와 한 사람 몫은 반비례해요.
examples.en: If the cake stays the same size, the number of people and each person's share are inversely proportional.

examples.ko: 가격과 수요가 꼭 반비례한다고 말할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't say that price and demand are always inversely related.

examples.ko: 노력과 성적이 반비례하면 공부 방법을 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: If your effort and grades move in opposite directions, you need to change how you study.

explain: '비례하다'(같이 늘고 줄다)의 반대로, 한쪽이 커질 때 다른 쪽이 작아지는 관계예요. 수학에서는 '정비례'와 짝으로 쓰고, 일상에서도 '둘은 반비례 관계예요'라고 말해요. 보통 'A와 B는 반비례하다'처럼 두 가지를 같이 말해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '비례하다' (rise and fall together): when one grows, the other shrinks. In math it pairs with '정비례', and in daily talk people say '둘은 반비례 관계예요'. You usually mention both things, as in 'A와 B는 반비례하다'.

examples.ko: 갑자기 공이 날아와서 반사적으로 고개를 숙였어요.
examples.en: A ball suddenly flew at me, and I ducked by reflex.
When I'm startled, I scream first, without thinking.
I answered 'I'm fine' automatically to that question.

examples.ko: 반사적인 행동이라서 저도 왜 그랬는지 몰라요.
examples.en: It was a reflex action, so I don't know why I did it either.
That's a reflexive reaction, so it's hard to change.
I laughed instinctively at the funny remark.

explain: 실제로는 '반사적으로', '반사적인 행동/반응'처럼 뒤에 붙여서 많이 써요. 생각할 틈 없이 몸이나 말이 먼저 나가는 상황에 쓰고, '무의식적으로'와 비슷해요. 좋고 나쁜 뜻은 없고 상황 설명에 써요.
explain_en: In practice it appears as '반사적으로' or '반사적인 행동/반응'. It describes the body or mouth acting before you can think, and is close to '무의식적으로' (unconsciously). It is neutral and just describes the situation.

examples.ko: 반사회적 행동이 늘어나서 학교에서 상담을 시작했어요.
examples.en: Antisocial behavior has increased, so the school started counseling.

examples.ko: 그런 반사회적인 생각은 혼자 키우지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't nurse that kind of antisocial thinking all by yourself.

examples.ko: 그는 일부러 반사회적으로 행동하려는 사람은 아니에요.
examples.en: He isn't someone who tries to act against society on purpose.
'Antisocial' is too harsh a thing to say.

examples.ko: 반사회적 성향이 있다고 단정하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't jump to the conclusion that someone has antisocial tendencies.

examples.ko: 사회가 불안하면 반사회적 분위기가 퍼지기 쉬워요.
examples.en: When society is uneasy, an antisocial mood spreads easily.

explain: '반사회적 행동/성향/분위기'처럼 사회의 규칙이나 질서에 맞서는 것을 말해요. '비사회적'은 사람을 잘 안 만나는 성격에 가까워서 달라요. 뉴스나 상담, 수업에서 자주 나오고 일상 대화에서는 조금 딱딱해요.
explain_en: It is used in '반사회적 행동/성향/분위기' for things that go against society's rules and order. '비사회적' is closer to being unsociable, so they differ. It appears in news, counseling and lessons, and sounds a bit stiff in daily talk.

examples.ko: 이번 달 반상회는 금요일 저녁에 있어요.
examples.en: This month's neighborhood meeting is on Friday evening.
We decided to talk about the parking problem at the neighborhood meeting.

examples.ko: 저는 바빠서 반상회에 못 갈 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm busy, so I don't think I can go to the neighborhood meeting.
After the neighborhood meeting ended, I had tea with the neighbors.

examples.ko: 우리 아파트는 반상회를 두 달에 한 번 해요.
examples.en: Our apartment complex holds a neighborhood meeting once every two months.
They posted the notice for the neighborhood meeting in the elevator.

explain: 한 동네나 아파트 단지의 이웃들이 모여 소식과 문제를 이야기하는 모임이에요. 보통 '반상회를 하다/열다', '반상회에 가다/참석하다'라고 해요. 아파트에서는 '입주민 회의'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a gathering where neighbors in a block or apartment complex talk about news and problems. People say '반상회를 하다/열다' and '반상회에 가다/참석하다'. In apartments it may also be called '입주민 회의' (residents' meeting).

examples.en: I lit up when I saw my friend after so long.
He just greeted me stiffly, without any sign of delight.
His delighted reaction made me feel good too.

examples.ko: 반색이 가득한 얼굴로 저를 맞아 주셨어요.
examples.en: She welcomed me with a face full of delight.

examples.ko: 제안을 했더니 팀장님이 뜻밖의 반색을 보였어요.
examples.en: When I made the suggestion, the team leader showed unexpected delight.
Even if it's not joy, I wish you'd at least smile.

explain: 반가운 사람이나 소식을 만났을 때 얼굴과 태도에 확 드러나는 기쁨이에요. 보통 '반색을 하다'나 동사 '반색하다'로 말해요. 기쁜 마음을 숨기지 않고 보여 주는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is the joy that shows clearly on your face and in your manner when you meet a welcome person or hear good news. It is usually said as '반색을 하다' or with the verb '반색하다'. It suggests not hiding your happiness.

examples.en: My younger sibling always lights up when getting pocket money.
The team leader was delighted to hear my suggestion.

examples.ko: 그 소식에 모두가 반색하며 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Everyone clapped happily at the news.
Seeing the delighted face, I was happy too.

examples.ko: 너무 반색할 일은 아니니까 차분히 기다려요.
examples.en: It's nothing to get too excited about, so let's wait calmly.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손녀를 보자마자 반색하고 안아 주셨어요.
examples.en: As soon as Grandma saw her granddaughter, she lit up and hugged her.

explain: 반가운 사람을 만나거나 기쁜 말을 들었을 때 기쁨이 바로 드러나는 모습에 써요. '기뻐하다'보다 그 순간의 표정과 반응이 눈에 보이는 느낌이에요. 높일 때는 '반색하셨어요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when joy shows right away on meeting a welcome person or hearing good words. Compared with '기뻐하다', you can almost see the expression and reaction at that moment. For honorifics, say '반색하셨어요'.

examples.en: At first I was half-skeptical about that ad.
I tried the medicine with mixed feelings of trust and doubt.

examples.ko: 그 이야기가 사실인지 저는 아직도 반신반의예요.
examples.en: I'm still half in doubt about whether that story is true.
I was unsure, but when I went myself, it was true.
Everyone waited for the result, torn between belief and doubt.

examples.ko: 반신반의인 사람이 많아서 설명이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: Many people are unsure, so more explanation is needed.

explain: 절반은 믿고 절반은 의심하는 마음을 말하는 사자성어예요. 보통 '반신반의하다'로 쓰고, 명사로는 '반신반의예요/반신반의였어요'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '긴가민가하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a four-character expression for half believing and half doubting. It is usually used as the verb '반신반의하다', and as a noun in forms like '반신반의예요/반신반의였어요'. In daily talk people also say '긴가민가하다'.

examples.en: I'm half in doubt about whether it will really work.
At first everyone was unsure about the plan.
Though I had doubts, I applied anyway.
Many people are unsure whether to believe that.
The price is so cheap that I can't help but doubt it.

examples.ko: 반신반의했는데 막상 해 보니 정말 좋았어요.
examples.en: I was unsure, but when I actually tried it, it was really good.

explain: 믿어도 될지 의심해야 할지 마음이 반반일 때 써요. '믿지 않다'처럼 완전히 부정하는 것이 아니라 확신이 안 서는 상태예요. 대화에서는 '긴가민가해요'가 더 편하게 들려요.
explain_en: Use it when you are split between trusting and doubting. It is not a flat disbelief but a state of not feeling sure. In conversation, '긴가민가해요' sounds more casual.

examples.en: We learned ironic expressions in Korean class.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 반어로 가득해서 읽는 재미가 있어요.
examples.en: This novel is full of irony, which makes it fun to read.

examples.ko: 친구의 칭찬이 반어법이라는 걸 나중에 알았어요.
examples.en: I later realized my friend's compliment was ironic.
You have to hear the tone as well to understand irony.
There was a question about finding irony on the exam.

examples.ko: 그 제목은 반어에 가까워서 처음엔 헷갈렸어요.
examples.en: The title is close to ironic, so I was confused at first.

explain: '반어법'으로 가장 많이 쓰고, 국어 수업이나 문학 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '비꼬다'처럼 말하고, 말투와 표정으로 속뜻을 알 수 있어요. 겉뜻과 속뜻이 반대일 때 '반어', 사실보다 크게 말하는 것은 '과장'이라서 달라요.
explain_en: It is used mostly as '반어법' and comes up in Korean class and talk about literature. In daily life people say things like '비꼬다' (to be sarcastic), and tone and expression reveal the real meaning. '반어' is for when the surface and real meanings are opposite, while '과장' (exaggeration) is saying more than the truth, so they differ.

examples.ko: 이 필터는 반영구적으로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this filter almost permanently.
If you want a long-lasting effect, consult a clinic.
Even if it's called semi-permanent, you still have to maintain it.

examples.ko: 이 도료는 반영구적 보호막을 만들어 줘요.
examples.en: This coating creates a long-lasting protective layer.

examples.ko: 저는 반영구적일 만큼 오래 쓰는 가방이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like bags that last almost forever.
It's not semi-permanent, but it lasts quite a while.

explain: 영원은 아니어도 아주 오래 가는 물건이나 효과에 써요. '반영구적으로 쓰다', '반영구적인 제품'처럼 쓰고 광고에도 자주 나와요. 완전한 '영구적'과 달리 언젠가 끝날 수 있다는 뜻이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It describes things or effects that are not forever but last a very long time. It is used as '반영구적으로 쓰다' and '반영구적인 제품', and shows up often in ads. Unlike fully '영구적' (permanent), it implies it may end someday.

examples.ko: 무리하게 다이어트를 하면 반작용으로 폭식하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you diet too hard, you easily binge as a backlash.

examples.ko: 힘을 주면 같은 크기의 반작용이 생겨요.
examples.en: When you apply force, a reaction of equal size is produced.

examples.ko: 강한 규제는 반작용을 부를 수 있어요.
examples.en: Strict regulation can cause a backlash.

examples.ko: 반작용 때문에 오히려 더 안 하게 되었어요.
examples.en: Because of the reaction, I ended up doing it even less.
I explained in advance to prepare for a backlash.

examples.ko: 그 정책은 큰 반작용 없이 받아들여졌어요.
examples.en: That policy was accepted without much backlash.

explain: 물리의 '작용·반작용'에서 왔지만, 일상에서는 어떤 일에 대해 반대로 나오는 반응을 말해요. '부작용'은 약이나 정책의 나쁜 부수 효과이고, 반작용은 눌린 쪽이 되돌아오는 반응이라서 달라요. '반작용이 생기다/크다', '반작용을 부르다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It comes from the physics pair 'action and reaction', but in daily life it means a response that pushes back against something. '부작용' is a bad side effect of medicine or a policy, while 반작용 is a counter-response from the pressured side, so they differ. Use it as '반작용이 생기다/크다' and '반작용을 부르다'.

examples.en: Our choir's accompanist is a piano teacher.
The accompanist suddenly got sick, so the performance was postponed.

examples.ko: 반주자를 구하는 광고를 학교 게시판에서 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an ad looking for an accompanist on the school bulletin board.

examples.ko: 노래할 때 반주자와 호흡을 맞추는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: When singing, it's important to be in sync with the accompanist.
I work as an accompanist at a church.
Please send the sheet music to the accompanist first.

explain: 노래나 춤 옆에서 피아노 같은 악기로 받쳐 주는 사람이에요. '반주를 하다'와 짝으로 외우면 좋아요. 곡 전체를 혼자 연주하는 사람은 '독주자'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: This is the person who backs up a song or dance with an instrument such as a piano. It is useful to learn it together with '반주를 하다'. Someone who plays a whole piece alone is a '독주자' (soloist), so they differ.

examples.en: I put oil on my hair, and now it's glossy.
My newly bought shoes are shining sleekly.
Don't be fooled by his slick way of talking.
The fur looks glossy and shiny.
I ate oily food, so my lips were shiny.
It's only shiny on the outside; it's empty inside.

explain: 윤기가 나고 매끈해 보일 때 써요. '번지르르하다'와 모음만 다른 비슷한 말로, 반지르르가 조금 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요. '겉만 반지르르하다'처럼 겉모습만 좋은 것을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Use it for something that looks shiny and smooth. It is a close relative of '번지르르하다' differing only in vowels, with 반지르르 feeling a bit smaller and lighter. It is also used for things that only look good outside, as in '겉만 반지르르하다'.

examples.en: Grandmother took a needle out of the sewing box.
A button fell off, so I looked for the sewing box.

examples.ko: 반짇고리 안에는 실과 가위가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: There are thread and scissors in the sewing box.

examples.ko: 반짇고리는 서랍장 맨 아래 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The sewing box is in the bottom drawer of the chest.
I didn't have a sewing box, so I borrowed a needle from a neighbor.
My mom's old sewing box is full of memories.

explain: 바늘, 실, 가위, 단추 같은 바느질 도구를 담아 두는 그릇이에요. 요즘 여행용 작은 세트는 '바느질 세트'라고도 해요. 'ㄷ' 받침이 있어서 쓸 때 '반짇고리'로 써야 하는 점을 주의하세요.
explain_en: It is a container that holds sewing tools such as needles, thread, scissors and buttons. A small travel set is nowadays also called a '바느질 세트' (sewing set). Watch the spelling: it is written with the 'ㄷ' batchim as '반짇고리'.

examples.en: The freshly polished floor is glossy.
My oily nose is shiny, and it bothers me.
Seeing the shiny shoes makes me feel good.

examples.ko: 오래 쓴 소매가 반질거려서 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: The sleeves I wore a long time got shiny, so I bought new ones.
When my face gets shiny, I use blotting paper.
After I polished it, the pot gleamed.

explain: 매끄럽고 윤이 나서 빛이 반사되는 모습이에요. 닦아서 깨끗해 보일 때도, 기름이 껴서 번들거릴 때도 써요. '반질반질'을 같이 외우면 좋고, '번들거리다'는 조금 더 크고 기름진 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes a smooth, glossy surface that reflects light. It can be used for something polished and clean, or for something oily and shiny. Learn it with '반질반질'; '번들거리다' feels a bit bigger and greasier.

examples.en: After I wiped the floor, it shines glossily.
The marbles were so glossy that I wanted them.
I polished my shoes until they shone and went to the interview.
I picked an apple with a glossy shine.
The railing has been worn smooth and shiny by many hands.
The baby's cheeks are glowing and smooth.

explain: 매끈하고 윤이 나는 모양을 소리처럼 흉내 낸 말이에요. 잘 닦은 물건에도, 오래 만져서 닳은 물건에도 써요. '반들반들'과 비슷하고, '윤이 나다'와 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It imitates the look of a smooth, shiny surface. It works for well-polished things and for things worn smooth by long handling. It is close to '반들반들' and often appears with '윤이 나다'.

examples.en: Every evening I reflect on my day.

examples.ko: 지난 실수를 반추하며 앞으로는 조심하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Reflecting on my past mistake, I decided to be careful from now on.

examples.ko: 면접이 끝나고 제 대답을 반추해 봤어요.
examples.en: After the interview, I went back over my answers.
Taking time to reflect helps sort out your feelings.

examples.ko: 과거를 너무 오래 반추하면 오히려 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you dwell on the past too long, it actually gets hard.
I looked back on this year while writing in my diary.

explain: 소가 먹은 것을 다시 씹는 '되새김질'에서 온 말이라, 지나간 일을 되풀이해서 생각한다는 느낌이 있어요. '되돌아보다'보다 글 같고 깊이 곱씹는 느낌이라, 말보다 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 들려요. 후회하며 계속 생각할 때는 '곱씹다'도 써요.
explain_en: It comes from the chewing of cud, so it carries a sense of going over past events again and again. It feels more literary and deeper than '되돌아보다' (look back), and is heard more in writing or presentations than in speech. For dwelling on something with regret, '곱씹다' is also used.

examples.ko: 올해 농사는 비 때문에 반타작이 됐어요.
examples.en: This year's harvest came out at only about half because of the rain.

examples.ko: 시험 준비를 못 해서 점수가 반타작이에요.
examples.en: I couldn't prepare for the exam, so I only got about half the score.
I'd be glad to finish even half of what I planned.
I think it's fortunate we at least got half.
This round of business ended up at only about half of what I hoped.
Even a half harvest is enough for my family to eat.

explain: 원래는 지주와 소작인이 거둔 곡식을 절반씩 나누는 일을 가리켰고, 지금은 농사나 일, 점수가 절반쯤밖에 안 될 때도 써요. 대체로 '기대보다 아쉽다'는 느낌이 들어 있어요. '반타작이 되다/하다'처럼 말하고 대화에서 편하게 나와요.
explain_en: It originally meant landlord and tenant splitting the harvest in half, and now it is also used when a harvest, work or score reaches only about half. It usually carries a sense of disappointment compared with expectations. It is said as '반타작이 되다/하다' and comes up easily in conversation.

examples.en: He laughs off even difficult questions.

examples.ko: 농담을 진담으로 받지 않고 가볍게 받아넘겼어요.
examples.en: I didn't take the joke seriously and brushed it off lightly.
She is good at fending off an opponent's attacks.
I was angry, but I decided to bear it and let it pass.
I was upset that I couldn't shrug off the teasing.
You can just deflect it, so don't worry too much.

explain: 상대가 던진 말이나 공격을 받고 크게 흔들리지 않고 넘기는 모습에 써요. 말에서는 '대수롭지 않게 넘기다'와 비슷하고, 같은 힘으로 날카롭게 되받는 '받아치다'와는 달라요. 공이나 물건을 받아서 다른 쪽으로 넘길 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes taking in what someone throws at you, whether words or attacks, and passing it on without being shaken. For words it is close to '대수롭지 않게 넘기다' (treat as no big deal), and differs from '받아치다', which means to hit back sharply. It can also be used for catching a ball or object and sending it on.

examples.en: A cow suddenly ran up, and a person got butted.
I almost got butted by a cow in a narrow alley.
I was butted by a goat and got a bruise on my arm.
The spot where I was hit still hurts.
Be careful that the child isn't butted by the cow.

examples.ko: 받히면 크게 다칠 수 있으니 멀리 떨어지세요.
examples.en: You can get badly hurt if you're butted, so stay far away.

explain: 소나 염소 같은 동물의 뿔이나 머리에 세게 부딪힐 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요. '바치다'와 발음이 같아서 글자를 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 차에 부딪힌 때는 보통 '치이다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: This is a passive form used when you are hit hard by an animal's horn or head, such as a cow's or goat's. It sounds the same as '바치다', so the spelling is easy to mix up. For being hit by a car, people more often say '치이다'.

examples.en: The child is running around naked to take a bath.

examples.ko: 발가벗은 채로 밖에 나가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not go outside without any clothes on.
The baby in the picture is cute even without clothes.

examples.ko: 꿈에서 발가벗는 장면을 보고 놀라서 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up startled after seeing myself naked in a dream.
I was undressed, so I quickly covered myself with a towel.
You'll be cold without clothes, so put something on.

explain: 옷을 다 벗은 상태를 말하고, '벌거벗다'와 거의 같아요. '발가-'는 작고 가벼운 느낌이고 '벌거-'는 큰 느낌이에요. 벗은 상태를 말할 때는 '발가벗은'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It describes being completely undressed and is nearly the same as '벌거벗다'. '발가-' feels smaller and lighter and '벌거-' feels bigger. For the state of being undressed, use '발가벗은'.

examples.en: He boasts outstanding skill on the team.
That player's performance was truly outstanding.
Her cooking skill is rumored to be exceptional.

examples.ko: 이번 경기에서 발군의 활약을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: He showed an outstanding performance in this game.
That new actor's acting ability is exceptional.
She is such a standout student that all the teachers remember her.

explain: 여럿 가운데 혼자 눈에 띄게 뛰어난 것을 말해요. 보통 '발군의 실력/활약/성적'처럼 '발군의'로 많이 쓰고, 뉴스나 칭찬하는 글에서 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '제일 잘하다', '훨씬 뛰어나다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes someone or something that stands out as excellent among many. It is mostly used as '발군의' in '발군의 실력/활약/성적', and often seen in news and praise. In daily talk people also say '제일 잘하다' or '훨씬 뛰어나다'.
